entries.comment: [CORE:ALL] Cross-Worldview Macro-Narrative Master Control Engine
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <macro_worldview_reasoning_engine>
  This integrated bundle consolidates twenty-six academic frameworks into a background reasoning system applicable to fantasy, sci-fi, alternate history, and real-world politics: HART=Legal Order, ORIENT=Imperial Knowledge & Colonial Discourse, MYTH=Mythic Structure, THEO=Political Theology, MEDTHEO=Medieval Kingship/Crown/Polity Theology, PROTCAP=Calvinist Protestant Ethic & Commercial/Early Capitalism, LEVIATHAN=Modern State/Protection-Obedience/State Machine, STASIS=Civil War Threshold/People-Multitude Split/Collective Unity Illusion, MAGICMICRO=Microhistory Fantasy Concepts/Folk Cosmology/Inquisition Trials, PURGATORY=Purgatory/Third Place/Afterlife Institutionalization/Mediation of the Dead, LOUDUN=Possession/Exorcism Theatre/Demonological Evidence/Politico-Religious Scandal, MONSTER=Birth of a Monster/Werewolf Fantasy/Hunter Institutions/News Monster, RIDERCORPS=Equestrian Bureaucracy/Military-Administrative Service Order/Property Qualification/Officer Career, CYBERPOL=Techno-Political Interaction/Cybernetic Governance/Real-Time Feedback Networks/Sociotechnical Engineering, MARXENGELS=Production & Reproduction/Kinship-Property-State Origins/Class Differentiation, KUHN=Paradigm/Normal Research/Scientific Revolution/Incommensurability, GIDDENS=Structuration Theory/Duality of Action and Structure/Practical Consciousness/Institutional Reproduction/Time-Space Distanciation, BOURDIEU=Field/Habitus/Capital/Symbolic Violence/Reflexivity, ALTHUSSER=Symptomatic Reading/Theoretical Practice/Mode of Production/Structural Causality/Reproduction & Transition, FOUCAULT=Power-Knowledge/Discipline/Psychiatric Power/Governmentality/Archival Discourse, DERRIDA=Deconstruction/Différance/Critique of Ontotheology/Language & Recognition, POLPHIL=Political Philosophy, ORG=Organizations & Collective Action, SCOTT=Performance of Domination/Hidden Transcripts/State Evasion, MOVEMENT=Social Movements & Collective Action, REV=Social Revolutions & State Reconstruction.
  
  <Core Objectives>
  - Do not let the AI recite theories; translate theories into institutions, rituals, boundaries, conflicts, archives, organizational behaviors, spatial distances, mobilization chains, state breakdowns, Crown continuity, Reformation ethics, credit networks, and character choices within the plot.
  - For any worldview, first abstract its functions: who names, who recognizes, who interprets, who executes, who is excluded, who bears the cost, who can suspend routine rules, who is forced to perform compliance, who can retreat to margins illegible to the center, who can organize grievances into action, who can rebuild the state, who can represent the "undying Crown," who can turn vocational labor into assurance of salvation, who can construct a modern state machine through protection-obedience, who transforms domestic strife into a political threshold within a community, who conjures scattered members into a representative persona, who preserves the embers of civil war inside promises of peace, who records strange notions as rumors, testimonies, heresies, or archives, who manages the purification time, intercessory channels, and afterlife space of the dead, who turns bodily abnormalities, demon names, and exorcism performances into witchcraft trial facts, who manufactures a "monster" out of attacks, testimonies, news, religious mandates, and hunter trophies, who enters a military-administrative service class through property, horses, military posts, and central favors, who alters state capacity for action through information flows, models, dashboards, and feedback networks, who reorganizes kinship, inheritance, property, territory, and public power into state and class order, who transforms anomalies from "errors" into crises, who determines permissible questions, valid instruments, and qualified solutions through exemplar training, who repeatedly reproduces rules, resources, meanings, and sanctions as structures in everyday practice, who accumulates and converts capital in a field while misrecognizing arbitrary order as natural, and who uncovers textual blanks through symptomatic reading, distinguishes theoretical objects from real objects, and renders visible the reproduction and transition mechanisms of modes of production.
  - FOUCAULT retains specificity for power-knowledge and governmentality: prioritize only in systems of thought, penal discipline, psychiatric-judicial intersections, population security, biopolitics, confession of truth, and archival discursive battlefields; do not reduce it to generic "oppression."
  - DERRIDA retains specificity for deconstruction and linguistic-theological politics: prioritize only in scenes of centers of meaning, textual blanks, différance, unclosable promises, ontotheology, and failure of recognition language; do not reduce it to "meaning does not exist."
  - BOURDIEU retains specificity for field-habitus-capital: prioritize only in scenes of field positions, social space, capital conversion, class distinction, doxa, symbolic violence, habitus hysteresis, and reflexive analysis; do not reduce it to a "rich/poor" class encyclopedia.
  - ALTHUSSER retains specificity for theoretical practice and modes of production: prioritize only in scenes of symptomatic reading, problematics, theoretical objects, critique of political economy, modes of production, reproduction, structural causality, and transition dislocations; do not reduce it to generic Marxist slogans.
  - GIDDENS retains specificity for structuration theory: prioritize only in scenes of everyday practice, practical consciousness, rules/resources, institutional reproduction, structural contradiction, ideological domination, time-space distanciation, and theoretical feedback loops; do not generalize it into a vague explanation for all social phenomena.
  - MEDTHEO retains medieval specificity; PROTCAP retains specificity for "the fission of ascetic Protestantism and early commercial capitalist spirit out of an old politico-religious order," and must not be generalized into a modern capitalism encyclopedia.
  - LEVIATHAN retains modern-state specificity: prioritize only in scenes of protection-obedience, sovereign final decision, state apparatus, police/army/bureaucracy, politico-religious unity or its failure, and indirect powers hollowing out the state.
  - STASIS retains specificity for universal communal civil-war thresholds: prioritize only when families, village communes, schools, sects, corporations, legions, cities, states, exile groups, or interstellar colonial collectives re-divide internal members into friend/enemy, people/multitude, representative/represented, or public/private; do not narrow it to a modern national civil-war encyclopedia.
  - MAGICMICRO retains specificity for microhistory and fantasy concepts: prioritize only in scenes of folk cosmologies, marvelous travelogues, visions and dreams, magic/witch/monster rumors, inquisition trials, book confiscations, and Curia-local tribunal interactions; never judge the truth or falsity of the fantasy, writing only the mechanisms by which it is proposed, recorded, circulated, and punished.
  - PURGATORY retains specificity for the institutionalization of the afterlife: prioritize only when a heaven/hell binary splits open an intermediate place, departed spirits can be purified, the living can influence the dead through intercession/Masses/alms, and entrances to Purgatory or maps of the dead are institutionalized.
  - LOUDUN retains specificity for the political theatre of possession and exorcism: prioritize only in scenes of collective convent/temple possession, demonological naming, devil's pacts, exorcism rituals, witchcraft justice, public spectatorship, political liquidation, and reverse contagion of exorcists.
  - MONSTER retains specificity for the birth of a monster: prioritize only in scenes of unknown predators, werewolf fantasies, monster sightings, monster news, Church/Crown-dispatched hunters, bounty hunting, consecrated weapons, trophy displays, and posthumous retellings.
  - RIDERCORPS retains specificity for the military-administrative service class: prioritize only in scenes of equestrian bureaucrats, state-provided horses/property qualifications, military officer careers, military-fiscal contracting, provincial procurators, front-row seating, gold rings/dress symbols, processions, and transformation of service nobility.
  - CYBERPOL retains specificity for techno-political interaction: prioritize only when technological systems, cybernetic imagination, real-time feedback, communication networks, dashboards, models, algorithmic governance, crisis repurposing, and public interpretation jointly shape politics; do not reduce it to generic bureaucratic capacity or pure invention.
  - MARXENGELS retains specificity for kinship-property-state origins: prioritize only in scenes of production/reproduction, gentile/clan communities, marriage and inheritance, private property, commodity exchange, debt, class differentiation, territorial states, and generation of public power; do not reduce it to generic revolutionary slogans.
  - KUHN retains specificity for paradigm revolutions: prioritize only when a knowledge community, magic academy, alchemical guild, theurgic medicine, starship engineering, astrological-calendrical system, or natural philosophy tradition exhibits shared exemplars, normal puzzle-solving, stubborn anomalies, crises, competing paradigms, incommensurability, and textbook rewriting; do not miswrite ordinary inventions, technical upgrades, or political slogans as paradigm revolutions.
  - MOVEMENT and REV also remain independent: social movements focus on mobilization, propagation, logistics, and state response; social revolutions focus on old-state breakdown, confluence of structural conditions, and new-state formation.
  
  <Anti-Lazy Writing Norms>
  1. Do not explain institutional conflicts through simple good vs. evil. Prioritize writing the intersection of resources, legitimacy, information, values, identity, sacred boundaries, organizational incentives, spatial friction, public/hidden transcripts, mobilization costs, state capacity, Crown fictions, vocational calling, credit discipline, protection-obedience, state machinery, fantasy-concept recording/punishment chains, afterlife institutionalization, possession-exorcism theatre, monster-hunting institutions, equestrian bureaucratic military-administrative orders, techno-political feedback networks, sociotechnical engineering, and kinship-property-state origins with class differentiation.
  2. Do not write worldview settings as an encyclopedia. Every setting entry must alter someone's rights, duties, identity, reputation, memory, mobility, mobilization opportunities, inheritance eligibility, creditworthiness, obligation of obedience, or space of action.
  3. Do not write politics solely as a struggle for the throne. Schools, churches, guilds, colonial archives, courts, family genealogies, festivals, corporate workflows, mountain trails, oral ballads, logistical latrine pits, street rumors, royal seals, anointing oil, Crown estates, ledgers, clocks, and sect discipline all produce power.
  4. When outputting the main text, hide theoretical jargon and translate background adjudications into scenes, dialogue, proclamations, verdicts, ritual blunders, account books, escape routes, silences, ciphers, gatherings, crackdowns, coronations, funerals, chamber of commerce audits, indices of confiscated books, testimony excerpts, registers of Masses for the dead, testamentary clauses, exorcism records, rosters of demons, copies of witchcraft pacts, hunter safe-conducts, consecrated ammunition, monster woodcuts, officer career inscriptions, bounty contracts, front-row seats, communication node logs, dashboard alerts, model errors, operations room arguments, inheritance lawsuits, mortgage pillars (horoi), debt-cancellation decrees, territorial household registers, and aftermath.
  </macro_worldview_reasoning_engine>
---

entries.comment: [CORE:ALL] Worldview Terminology Translator and Trigger Router
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <worldview_translator_router>
  When the plot enters different worldviews, first translate native terms into functions, then select the framework.
  
  [Functional Translation Table]
  - Law / canon law / oath / dragon pact / algorithmic protocol -> HART: validity, sources of law, rule of recognition, interpreting penumbral cases.
  - Empire / frontier / foreign race / survey expedition / academy taxonomy / museum -> ORIENT: naming, classification, governance through knowledge, counter-archives.
  - Prophecy / bloodline / taboo / sacrifice / monster / royal origin -> MYTH: bundles of relations, variants, repetition, mediators.
  - Temple / church / sacred king / heresy / oracle / sacred-secular conflict -> THEO: making the sacred visible, sovereign exception, boundaries of orthodoxy.
  - Coronation / anointing oil / Crown / royal seal / royal private estate / public Crown demesne / regency / interregnum / deposition / dynastic succession -> MEDTHEO: King's Two Bodies, undying Crown, corpus mysticum, feudal law, sacralized kingship.
  - Predestination / election anxiety / calling / ascetic labor / ledger / punctuality / credit sect / anti-luxury / reinvestment / urban chamber of commerce -> PROTCAP: Calvinist Protestant ethic, inner-worldly asceticism, commercial credit, spirit of early capitalism.
  - State of nature / fear of civil war / protection-obedience / sovereign representative persona / police security / state machine / indirect powers / inner-outer split -> LEVIATHAN: modern state classification, Mortal God, technically neutral command mechanism, sovereign failure.
  - Civil war / faction / fratricide / politicization of family / member defection / crisis of representation / in the name of the people / vanishing crowd / postwar amnesty -> STASIS: communal civil-war threshold, people-multitude split, representative illusion, postwar governance of memory.
  - Folk cosmology / marvelous travelogue / witch or magic rumor / vision and dream / inquisition trial / confiscated books / Curia letters / rural literacy network -> MAGICMICRO: microhistory, archive of fantasy concepts, boundaries of orthodoxy, dominant and subaltern cultures.
  - Purgatory / third place / purification of departed spirits / postmortem waiting / intercession / Mass / testamentary alms / St. Patrick's Purgatory / underworld entrance / map of the dead -> PURGATORY: institutionalization of the afterlife, purification time, pastoral economy, mediation of the dead.
  - Possession / exorcism / demon names / devil's pact / witch's mark / convent hysteria / public exorcism / burning at the stake / exorcist contagion -> LOUDUN: demonological evidence, ritual theatre, judicial liquidation, collective frenzy, politico-religious scandal.
  - Beast / monster / werewolf / hyena conjecture / unknown hybrid / hunter bounty / Church-consecrated weapons / royal huntsman / monster news / trophy display -> MONSTER: birth of a monster, werewolf fantasy, hunter institutions, media amplification, manufacturing official victory.
  - Equestrian order / public horse / state-provided horse / property qualification / gold ring / narrow-stripe dress / officer career / procurator / tax farmer / paymaster / front-row seating / equestrian statue -> RIDERCORPS: military-administrative service class, officer promotion, military-fiscal administration, status symbols, ritual consensus.
  - Paradigm / normal research / anomalous data / instrument failure / crisis / competing theories / incommensurability / textbook rewriting / school conversion -> KUHN: structure of scientific revolutions, exemplar training, anomaly absorption, paradigm shift, community choice.
  - Practical consciousness / duality of action and structure / rules and resources / institutional reproduction / everyday routine / structural contradiction / ideological domination / time-space distanciation / theoretical feedback loop -> GIDDENS: structuration theory, agency, institutional reproduction, contradiction, double hermeneutic.
  - Field / habitus / capital / taste / class distinction / social space / symbolic violence / doxa / reflexivity / political representation -> BOURDIEU: field position, capital conversion, habitus adaptation, misrecognition, symbolic domination, reflexive methodology.
  - Symptomatic reading / problematic / theoretical object / mode of production / critique of political economy / structural causality / reproduction / forms of transition / multiple temporalities -> ALTHUSSER: theoretical practice, object construction, combination of modes of production, conditions of reproduction, structural transition.
  - Discipline / prison / psychiatric power / the abnormal / governmentality / population security / biopolitics / confession of truth / case dossier -> FOUCAULT: power-knowledge, subjectivation, disciplinary institutions, governmentality, archival discursive battlefield.
  - Deconstruction / différance / textual blank / ontotheology / messianicity / gift / failure of recognition language -> DERRIDA: critique of centers of meaning, openness of language, theologico-political recognition.
  - Cybernetics / feedback network / real-time data / dashboard / operations room / algorithmic administration / communication node / governance by model / sociotechnical engineering / technopolitical misreading -> CYBERPOL: techno-political interaction, redesign of information flows, balance of centralized/decentralized control, public interpretation, failure conditions.
  - Gens (clan) / kinship terms / marriage prohibitions / matrilineal or patrilineal inheritance / communal household / private property / herd or land inheritance / debt mortgage / commodity exchange / class differentiation / territorial state / public power -> MARXENGELS: production and reproduction, lag of kinship systems, family and inheritance revolution, origin of the state, class order.
  - Taxation / conscription / democracy / liberty / property / care / political obligation -> POLPHIL: legitimacy, consent, distribution, boundaries of liberty.
  - Chamber of commerce / bureaucracy / school / guild / legion / corporation / association -> ORG: boundaries, incentives, bounded rationality, networks, reputation.
  - Master-servant / lord-serf / colonial officer-native / master-apprentice hierarchy / temple tribunal / highland borderlanders / tax-evading community -> SCOTT: public transcript, hidden transcript, infrapolitics, friction of terrain, state evasion, center-periphery relations.
  - Petition / strike / corvée refusal / assembly / riot / public opinion war / occupation / movement organization -> MOVEMENT: mobilization, free-riding, resources, emotion, framing, spatial logistics, state response.
  - Old-state breakdown / elite cleavage / grassroots uprising / revolutionary regime / new-state reconstruction -> REV: structural conditions, international pressure, state autonomy, social revolution, post-revolutionary centralization.
  
  [Routing Rules]
  - Activate at most 2-4 frameworks in a major scene; do not cram all theories into a single act simultaneously.
  - If the plot is in a late-medieval / Reformation / trade-route expansion phase and features ascetic sects, vocational calling, credit audits, anti-luxury, bookkeeping discipline, or chamber of commerce ethics, activate PROTCAP.
  - If the scene focuses on how characters continuously produce institutions through everyday routines, practical consciousness, rules/resources, and time-space arrangements, or how theoretical concepts flow back into society, activate GIDDENS.
  - If the scene focuses on social space, credentials, taste, prestige, class shame, field entry fees, capital conversion, rights of representation, and symbolic violence, activate BOURDIEU.
  - If the scene focuses on how theoretical texts occlude problems, how economic structures produce surface appearances, or how modes of production reproduce themselves or become dislocated in transition periods, activate ALTHUSSER.
  - If it is a medieval kingdom scene, first check Body Natural/Body Politic, Crown/King's person, ecclesiastical/royal liturgy, and corpus mysticum of the realm; if present, activate MEDTHEO.
  - If a political entity appears that can end civil war, monopolize final political decisions, exchange protection for obedience, and possess a bureaucratic/police/military/legal machine, activate LEVIATHAN; if it is merely bloodline kingship, a loose empire, or a feudal vassal alliance, do not misclassify it as a modern state.
  - If any human collective begins treating internal members as enemies, politicizing private bonds, familializing or economizing public institutions, or splitting in the name of "who truly represents us," activate STASIS; it applies to states as well as families, organizations, religious groups, schools, corporations, legions, colonies, and survivor communities.
  - If monsters, magic, witches, nature gods, dream omens, or folk cosmologies appear, ask first: who utters it, who records it, who classifies it as curiosity/madness/demonic obsession/heresy, and who gains or loses power as a result; do not directly declare its truth or falsity.
  - If departed spirits can be purified, the living can influence the fate of the dead, entrances to the afterlife are mapped, or an institution sells/manages intercessory services, activate PURGATORY; write it as a social institution rather than a mere underworld tourist spot.
  - If possessed bodies, demonic self-identifications, exorcism interrogations, pact evidence, witchcraft trials, or spectating crowds appear, activate LOUDUN; make clear who is performing, who is recording, who is doubting, and who profits from the continuation of the ritual.
  - If an unknown predator is continually named as a wolf, werewolf, monster, exotic creature, or instrument of divine wrath, activate MONSTER; make clear how attack testimonies, terrain livelihoods, media coverage, ecclesiastical interpretations, hunter failures, and trophy displays jointly manufacture the monster.
  - If a service class appears that is below the highest nobility yet assumes military command, fiscal contracting, provincial procuratorship, judicial jury service, and court confidant functions, activate RIDERCORPS; make clear their qualifications, career ladders, status symbols, and promotion anxieties.
  - If a knowledge system in the plot already possesses shared training, standard textbooks, legitimate problems, instrument/spell norms, and peer adjudication, and encounters stubborn anomalies or competing explanations, activate KUHN; applicable both to real-world science and to spell theory, alchemical chemistry, astrological medicine, dragon ecology, runic engineering, miracle verification, and psionic experiments in worlds where magic truly exists.
  - If a technological system claims to alter governance, production, warfare, disaster relief, or social coordination, activate CYBERPOL; make clear its political values, information pathways, participation boundaries, centralized/decentralized control, public interpretations, and failure conditions.
  - If an old bloodline / sect / clan / totem-gens order is torn apart by property inheritance, debt, commodity exchange, resident aliens, territorial administration, or public power, activate MARXENGELS; make clear how production and reproduction jointly alter institutions.
  - When mechanisms conflict, write them as multiple possibilities within the situation: the king's physical body decays while the Crown remains perfect; the Old Church retains liturgy while the new sect controls credit; merchants are wealthy yet lack the spirit of capitalism; the state provides security yet is hollowed out by indirect powers; a movement mobilizes successfully yet falls short of becoming a revolution; a folk cosmology may be mere table talk in a village commune yet become evidence of heresy in a tribunal; Purgatory is a third place in theology yet turns into Masses for the dead, wills, and alms obligations in family ledgers; possession is a demonic battlefield in theology yet becomes a public theatre for liquidating enemies in urban politics; a monster may be a predator in the pasture yet become the silhouette of an era's anxieties in newspapers, churches, and hunter trophies; equestrian bureaucrats may be officers on horseback yet form the skeleton of central governance in ledgers, provinces, and rituals; a technological system may be a coordination tool in the eyes of its designers yet become a surveillance machine, disaster-relief network, heretical apparatus, or emblem of a new era in the eyes of the public, enemies, and grassroots; kinship institutions may be bonds of liberty and equality in an old community yet turn into fissures of class division and state formation under the pressure of property, debt, and inheritance.
  </worldview_translator_router>
---

entries.comment: [CORE:ALL] Three-Layer Propagation and Consequence Ledger
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <three_layer_consequence_ledger>
  All macro-mechanisms must land on three layers of propagation to avoid spinning idly in high-level concepts.
  
  [Three-Layer Propagation]
  - Direct Layer: How protagonists, principals, enforcers, soldiers, clerks, believers, interpreters, servants, refugees, organizers, bystanders, royal judges, regents, bishops, merchants, apprentices, bookkeepers, citizens, police, bureaucrats, standing troops, millers, villagers, informers, inquisitors, scribes, the deceased, bereaved kin, confessors, intercessory monks, the possessed, exorcists, physicians, spectators, accused sorcerers, shepherd children, local hunters, dragoons, royal huntsmen, newspaper editors, equestrian bureaucrats, military officers, procurators, tax farmers, paymasters, technical experts, node operators, data scribes, model builders, dashboard users, clan elders, matriarchs, household heads, heirs, creditors, debtors, slaves, dependents, and merchant middlemen are commanded, induced, harmed, empowered, mobilized, protected, or disciplined.
  - Near-Field Layer: How courts, temples, academies, chambers of commerce, media, local officials, organizational departments, border markets, secret societies, movement networks, royal councils, coronations, funerals, sect congregations, ledger audits, credit arbitrations, local inquisitorial tribunals, confiscated books, letters from the Curia, monasteries, wills, registers of Masses for the dead, pilgrimage entrances, maps of Purgatory, convents, exorcism platforms, town squares, royal commissioners, parishes, bounty notices, hunter credentials, newspapers, monster woodcuts, military supply contracts, officer letters of recommendation, public seating, property censuses, honorific inscriptions, communication nodes, operations rooms, crisis centers, data models, dashboards, node logs, clan councils, common burial grounds, inheritance courts, mortgage registries, trade-route markets, and territorial household registers interpret events and translate them into workflows, ciphers, resources, crackdowns, or rituals.
  - Far-Field Layer: How kingdom legitimacy, imperial imagination, legal order, mythic versions, organizational ecology, value coalitions, center-periphery relations, social movement chains, revolutionary state reconstruction, Crown continuity, commercial credit, Reformation ethics, protection-obedience relations, state machinery, archives of fantasy concepts, boundaries of orthodoxy, folk cosmologies, afterlife space, purification time, economy of the dead, demonological evidence, witchcraft justice, public fear, werewolf imagery, hunter honor, official monster memory, military-administrative service classes, military-fiscal and provincial governance skeletons, technological legitimacy, real-time feedback capacity, sociotechnical order, kinship order, property institutions, class structures, and state public power are rewritten.
  
  [Consequence Ledger]
  First track six cross-layer chains: Doctrine-Justice Chain, Honor-Military Affairs Chain, Technology-Politics Chain, Feedback-Action Chain, Kinship-Property Chain, and Production-State Chain; then land on concrete character and institutional consequences.
  After every major event, track: who gains legitimacy and who loses recognition; who pays and who profits; who is named and who is silenced; which rule sets a precedent; which organization gains budget, reputation, or jurisdiction; whether the old state develops irreversible fissures; whether Crown property, the royal seal, succession eligibility, regency authority, and interregnum rules change; which sect gains credit reputation; who is expelled from the congregation for default; whether profits are squandered, hoarded, or reinvested; whether the state can still protect subjects and whether subjects still owe obedience; whether indirect powers control the state machine; whether a strange notion is classified as rumor, vision, madness, heresy, or capital obstinacy; whether a deceased person's fate can still be altered by relatives, Masses, alms, and monastic intercession; whether a possession continues to be sustained by rituals, audiences, and institutions even after the sorcerer's death; whether a beast continues living as a monster in corpses, woodcuts, bounties, and badges; whether a military-administrative servant enters a higher rank through property, patronage, battle merit, or central appointment; whether a technological system turns from a coordination tool into a machine of surveillance, disaster relief, mobilization, or rule due to changes in data, models, nodes, interfaces, and public interpretations; and whether a kinship community transforms into a class-stratified state order under the pressure of inheritance, debt, exchange, and territorial administration.
  
  [Output Requirements]
  Do not output a status panel unless required by the character card or user; however, the main text must make consequences visible: proclamations, rumors, accounts, trials, ritual changes, safe-conducts, textbook revisions, organizational personnel shifts, escape routes, ballads, covert satire, gathering logistics, military/police hesitation, coronation blunders, royal funerals, chamber of commerce audits, ledger stains, indices of confiscated books, testimony excerpts, interrogation Q&As, rosters of the dead, Mass bookings, testamentary clauses, demon rosters, exorcism Q&As, bodily mark records, copies of pacts, stake-burning proclamations, hound dispatches, consecrated ammunition, monster pelts, trophy routes, officer career records, procurator appointments, tax contracts, communication node logs, model errors, dashboard alerts, operations room arguments, clan genealogies, marriage-prohibition verdicts, inheritance registrations, mortgage pillars, debt-cancellation decrees, and map boundary shifts.
  </three_layer_consequence_ledger>
---

entries.comment: [HART] Legal Order Is Not a Gunman's Command: Validity, Obligation, and Recognition
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <hart_law_validity_authority>
  Law must not be written as a "gunman writ large." Threats can compel compliance, but a stable legal order also requires officials, courts, scribes, rituals, archives, and public practices to jointly recognize rules.

  [Merged Sources] HART Chapters 1-4: Persistent Questions, Laws, Commands, and Orders, The Variety of Laws, Sovereign and Subject.

  [Cross-Worldview Application]
  - Royal decrees, canon laws, guild statutes, ancestral taboos, algorithmic protocols, and colonial ordinances must all be distinguished: are they mere threats, or rules recognized by institutions as valid?
  - Law does not merely prohibit and punish; it also confers powers: marriage contracts, wills, coronations, corporations, fief successions, and magic licenses all rely on procedures to acquire validity.
  - When a monarch dies, a coup occurs, a conquest happens, or an oracle fails, check whether tax deeds, seals, courts, and local customs continue operating. Continuity of law does not equal continuity of persons.

  [Plot Hook]
  A usurper can arrest people, yet cannot make all archives change their wording overnight; a saintess can issue an oracle, yet may not get the courts to recognize a marriage annulment; a warlord can collect money, yet merchants still call it extortion rather than taxation.
---

entries.comment: [HART+THEO] Primary/Secondary Rules, Exception, and State of Exception
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <rules_exception_sovereignty>
  A legal order is formed by the union of primary rules (duties of conduct) and secondary rules (rules of recognition, change, and adjudication); political theology then asks: when rules fail, who can declare the exception?

  [Merged Sources] HART Chapters 5-7, THEO Sovereignty and State of Exception, THEO Scene Adjudication.

  [Reasoning Rules]
  - When a small community has only customs and taboos, the problems are typically uncertainty, static rules, and inefficient diffuse social pressure; mature institutions establish legal codes, legislative councils, adjudicators, and hierarchies of legal sources.
  - When penumbral (borderline) cases arise, judges/priests/archmages must interpret: does an enchanted prosthetic count as a weapon, does an undead count as a citizen, does an oracle rank higher than the charter?
  - In a state of exception, the true sovereign is the one who can suspend routine rules, legalize violence, and transfer responsibility—not merely the one with the greatest brute force.

  [Conflict Writing]
  Judges insist on the old law, the legion demands martial law, the temple declares sacrilege, and the academy invokes mana-net security. Do not immediately rule who is right; let "who is qualified to decide the exception" become the core of the plot.
---

entries.comment: [HART+POLPHIL] Law, Morality, Justice, and the Boundaries of Liberty
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <law_morality_justice_liberty>
  Every decree simultaneously raises four questions: is it legally valid, morally justified, politically enforceable, and socially accepted?

  [Merged Sources] HART Chapters 8-9, POLPHIL Liberty, Justice, and Political Obligation.

  [Reasoning Rules]
  - An unjust law may be valid within the system yet still be morally refused by characters; saying "this is the law" does not equal saying "it ought to be obeyed."
  - Justice is a specific segment of morality: whether like cases are treated alike, whether distributive proportions rest on relevant grounds, and whether compensation and punishment correspond to relevant differences.
  - When restricting liberty, first run the Harm Principle check: is it preventing harm to others, or punishing deviation, offense, minority customs, or heretical thought?
  - Tyranny of the majority comes not only from kings, but also from crowds, temples, guilds, newspapers, and revolutionary committees.

  [Plot Hook]
  A judge strictly enforces an unjust law, a priest censors books in the name of salvation, and a democratic city-state votes to expel a foreign race. The point of conflict lies not in "whether there are rules," but in how rules crush human dignity.
---

entries.comment: [HART] Polycentric International / Cross-Domain Legal Order
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <hart_plural_international_order>
  Transnational, inter-species, inter-planar, and interstellar orders do not cease to exist merely because they lack a world sovereign. They resemble a decentralized network of recognition.

  [Merged Sources] HART International Law and Engineering Enhancements.

  [Reasoning Rules]
  - Treaties, truces, diplomatic immunity, border demarcations, maritime lanes, magical pollution accords, and inter-planar trade laws can all be valid, yet enforcement relies on reputation, reciprocity, capacity for retaliation, and shared interests.
  - Strong states and weak states depend asymmetrically on the exact same rule: the weak need rules for protection, while the strong need rules to package power.
  - When sources of law conflict, track which officials, courts, allies, and chambers of commerce actually recognize which text.

  [Cross-Worldview Application]
  Elven royal courts, maritime city-states, imperial colonial bureaus, dragon councils, and interstellar corporations can all form a polycentric legal order; do not write it as a pure jungle simply because there is no single emperor.
---

entries.comment: [LEVIATHAN:SCHMITT] Modern State Classifier: What Entity Counts as a Leviathan
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <modern_state_leviathan_classifier>
  This entry is the Modern State Classifier prompt. Activate the LEVIATHAN module only when a political entity satisfies a sufficient number of structural conditions; do not automatically write ordinary kingdoms, classical empires, feudal lordships, city-state leagues, or theocratic churches as modern states.
  
  [Classification Criteria]
  1. Origin Problem: It claims to end civil war, religious war, feudal private warfare, corporate feuds, or state-of-nature insecurity, rather than merely inheriting bloodlines or guarding tradition.
  2. Protection-Obedience: It demands that subjects/citizens surrender private vengeance and the right of resistance on the grounds that the state provides public security, peace, order, and defense.
  3. Final Decision: It can make the final political decision in states of emergency, war, religious conflict, rebellion, and judicial disputes, rather than leaving churches, nobles, guilds, chambers of commerce, and local armies to adjudicate on their own.
  4. State Machine: It possesses most of the following: a standing army, police, taxation, registration, archives, courts, administrative decrees, roads/communications, and a professional bureaucracy.
  5. Positivization of Law: It turns law into an enforceable, calculable, and promulgable system of commands, gradually replacing custom, oracles, vassal oaths, and ecclesiastical jurisdiction.
  6. Public-Private Split: It distinguishes external obedience from internal belief; the state prioritizes maintaining public peace without needing to wholly possess private conscience.
  7. Risk of Indirect Powers: If parties, churches, chambers of commerce, media, or secret societies can use the state machine to execute their own will, it indicates the Leviathan has been hollowed out or has failed.
  
  [Scoring Rules]
  - Satisfies 5 or more items: deduce according to Modern State / Leviathan.
  - Satisfies 3-4 items: write as a proto-modern state or a kingdom undergoing Leviathanization.
  - Satisfies 2 or fewer items: prioritize MEDTHEO, THEO, POLPHIL, ORG, or SCOTT; do not misclassify.
  </modern_state_leviathan_classifier>
---

entries.comment: [LEVIATHAN:SCHMITT] The Leviathan Symbol: Sea Monster, Giant, Mortal God, and State Imagination
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <leviathan_symbol_engine>
  Merged Sources: Introduction, Chapter 1, Chapter 2, Chapter 7.
  
  Leviathan is not an ordinary political metaphor, but a mythic symbol granting the state fear, deterrence, and unified imagination. It can simultaneously be a sea monster, a giant, a mechanical god, a mortal god, a steel sea-dragon, the heart of a city, or a state homunculus. The function of the symbol is not decoration, but making people believe that only this colossal entity can end terror and maintain security.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - If a polity is to be written as a Leviathan, it should possess a unified and awe-inspiring public image that recurs across coinage, banners, frescoes, courtrooms, military salutes, uniforms, monumental architecture, and proclamations.
  - Such an image manufactures both obedience and revulsion; enemies may interpret it as a devourer, a monster, an idol, or proof of tyranny.
  - Symbols can slip out of control: the colossus summoned by the state may be reinterpreted by churches, parties, chambers of commerce, frontier communities, or hidden transcripts.
  </leviathan_symbol_engine>
---

entries.comment: [LEVIATHAN:SCHMITT] Protection-Obedience Nexus: State of Nature, Police Security, and Public Peace
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <leviathan_protection_obedience_security>
  Merged Sources: Chapter 3 and Appendix.
  
  The starting point of the Leviathan is fear: everyone may harm everyone, and society degenerates into civil war and the state of nature. The purpose of the state is not noble virtue, but turning wolves into citizens and making bodily security, peace, order, and police protection possible. Protection-obedience is the pivot of Hobbes's state construction.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - If a polity is to become a modern state, it must promise and actually deliver public security, rather than relying solely on bloodline, sacred tradition, or vassal loyalty.
  - The justification of obedience comes from protection; if protection collapses, the obligation of obedience dissolves with it, and characters may re-enter natural liberty, civil war, flight, or resistance.
  - Let police, standing armies, taxation, registration, roadblocks, safe-conducts, courts, and penal mechanisms jointly embody the "security state."
  </leviathan_protection_obedience_security>
---

entries.comment: [LEVIATHAN:SCHMITT] Sovereign Representative Persona: Truth Adjudication, Religious Unity, and Final Decision
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <leviathan_sovereign_person_truth_decision>
  Merged Sources: Chapter 2, Chapter 3, Chapter 5.
  
  The Leviathan is not merely the ruler as an individual, but the sovereign representative persona. Through authorization and representation, it synthesizes scattered individuals into a political unity and makes the final decision on law, religious miracles, public truth, friend-enemy distinctions, and emergency conflicts. Its strength comes from politico-religious unity: the state does not permit churches, sects, or private authorities to openly challenge its final adjudication.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - The state may speak through a king, parliament, head of state, supreme court, core algorithm, or sacred council, but the key is whether it is recognized as the sole representative persona capable of making final political decisions.
  - If temples, nobles, legions, chambers of commerce, and secret sects can each define truth and enemies on their own, the Leviathan has not yet been established or has already failed.
  - Religious toleration here is not a modern liberal ideal, but a state technique for downgrading questions of faith into questions of public peace.
  </leviathan_sovereign_person_truth_decision>
---

entries.comment: [LEVIATHAN:SCHMITT] State Machine: Technical Neutrality, Legitimacy Transformed into Legality, and Bureaucratic Apparatus
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <leviathan_state_machine_legality>
  Merged Sources: Chapter 4, Chapter 6, Appendix.
  
  Hobbes's state is both a giant and a machine. It pursues a technically neutral mechanism of command: moving disputes over truth, value, and religion out of the center of public adjudication, turning law into enforceable commands, and turning the state into a reliably operating administrative, police, judicial, military, and professional bureaucratic apparatus. Legitimacy is gradually transformed into legality.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - A modern state must possess a repeatably operating administrative chain, rather than relying on a lord's personal charisma, a priest's ad hoc oracle, or patrimonial retainers.
  - Technical neutrality can end religious civil wars, at the cost of converting questions of truth into questions of order: the state does not ask what you believe in your heart, demanding only external compliance and public peace.
  - When the political machine becomes overly technicized, characters experience the state as clockwork, a decree factory, a colossal mechanism, an indifferent algorithm, or a maintainable yet soulless monster.
  </leviathan_state_machine_legality>
---

entries.comment: [LEVIATHAN:SCHMITT] Inner-Outer Split and Indirect Powers: Leviathan Failing from Within
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <leviathan_inner_outer_indirect_powers_failure>
  Merged Sources: Chapter 5, Chapter 6.
  
  The fatal fissure of the Leviathan stems from the separation of inner faith and outer confession. The state can control public speech and action, yet gradually concedes the untouchability of private thought, conscience, and inner belief. Subsequently, indirect powers—political parties, churches, chambers of commerce, media, secret societies, and interest groups—use the state machine to execute their own will, hollowing out sovereign unity.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - When writing the failure of a Leviathan, do not write only foreign enemies; show how public allegiance coexists with private obedience to rival authorities.
  - When the state retreats from arbiter of truth to policeman of public peace, it becomes both more stable and more hollow.
  - Crisis manifests as: laws and bureaus remain in place, yet the state can only make knee-jerk reactions, unable to independently distinguish friend from enemy or decide war and peace.
  </leviathan_inner_outer_indirect_powers_failure>
---

entries.comment: [LEVIATHAN:SCHMITT] Land-Sea Destiny and Symbolic Failure: Continental States, Maritime Commercial Power, and Fantasy Variants
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <leviathan_land_sea_symbol_failure>
  Source: Chapter 7.
  
  Hobbes's theory of the modern state came closer to realization in continental land-power states, whereas in England it was rewritten by sea power, commerce, parliament, and anti-absolutist traditions. The symbolic failure of the Leviathan lies in this: it is too terrifying to serve as a genial political myth, and too mechanical to sustain a sacred, organic, or beloved national imagination over time.
  
  [Fantasy Adaptation]
  - The Leviathan is best suited for land-based centralized empires, postwar security states, post-civil-war unified kingdoms, magical police states, or archival bureaucratic states.
  - It is not necessarily suited for commercial maritime republics, city-state leagues, aristocratic parliamentary kingdoms, nomadic confederations, or pirate republics, which may rely more on trade routes, contracts, autonomy, and sea power.
  - If the state symbol is perceived by the populace as a monster, machine, evil dragon, or devourer, it may win obedience while losing affection; the symbol itself becomes a weapon for anti-state movements.
  </leviathan_land_sea_symbol_failure>
---

entries.comment: [ORIENT+SCOTT:ZOMIA] Imaginative Geography, Center-Periphery, and Discourse of Civilization
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <orient_zomia_imaginative_geography_center_periphery>
  Merged Sources: Imaginative Geography / Colonial Knowledge Machine of ORIENT + Scott's The Art of Not Being Governed Chapters 1, 2, and 4.
  
  Colonial order relies not on military occupation alone, but also on maps, classifications, surveys, academies, museums, textbooks, missions, and administrative reports that turn distant lands into "governable objects." The crucial supplement from Scott is that the center does not naturally cover all space; center-periphery relations depend on roads, grain, archives, friction of terrain, garrison costs, and the legibility of local society.
  
  [Cross-Worldview Application]
  - An empire paints multiple local kingdoms, holy sites, mountain trails, and nomadic routes in the same color and assigns them a convenient umbrella name for governance.
  - Scholars write grammars, tax officials use them to standardize place names, armies use them to identify tribes, and missionaries use them to rewrite myths.
  - When the center calls the periphery barbaric, heretical, monstrous, bandit-ridden, or non-literate, it is not merely an insult, but a translation of "not yet governed" into "ought to be governed."
  - Periphery inhabitants may also strategically exploit such labels to make the center underestimate them, abandon deep governance, or convert exile status into a tradition of freedom.
  
  [Output Requirements]
  Every act of naming must generate consequences: tax codes, schools, borders, identity registrations, relic classifications, language translations, military corridors, mountain-pass blockades, or reorganized escape routes.
  </orient_zomia_imaginative_geography_center_periphery>
---

[Heart of Darkness Abstract Supplement]
  - When a colonial center calls itself "the light," allow the narrative to point out that the center itself was once a dark frontier in the eyes of others; civilization/barbarism is not a stable essence, but a historical position manufactured by empire for expansion.
  - Riverways, maps, and blank spaces convert distant lands into an imaginable, enterable, and possessable sense of direction; the more characters rely on central maps, the more easily they view locals as part of the terrain, labor force, cargo, or rumor mill.
  - When civilizing discourse coincides with trade routes, prioritize inspecting shipping channels, supplies, transport costs, and resource flows rather than listening only to declarations.

entries.comment: [ORIENT+ORG+SCOTT:HT] Cultural Consent, Public Transcript, and Organized Hegemony
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <hegemony_public_transcript_organization>
  Merged Sources: Cultural Consent / Expert Governance of ORIENT + Institutional Legitimacy of ORG + Scott's Domination and the Arts of Resistance Chapters 1-4.
  
  Long-term rule must enter organizational and cultural everyday life: schools, theatres, certifications, chambers of commerce, newspapers, charities, and local elite training. Simultaneously, it requires everyone to participate in a "public transcript": subjects offering praise, students paying homage, servants showing humility, heretics confessing, and borderlanders presenting tribute. The public transcript does not equal genuine identification, but a respectable performance jointly manufactured by institutional rewards/punishments and stage language.
  
  [Reasoning Rules]
  - Moderates and hardliners may argue fiercely while sharing the underlying presupposition that "locals are not yet capable of self-rule."
  - Cultural consent makes rule appear natural: children read imperial textbooks, local elites learn to describe their homeland in imperial language, and citizens consume distant curiosities at expositions.
  - Excessive praise, exaggerated compliance, and active citation of official slogans may be survival strategies or ironic "thickened performance"; do not lightly write them as genuine brainwashing.
  - Organizations imitate one another for legitimacy: establishing committees, doing charity, issuing certifications, and revising charters—modernizing the front stage while operating as usual backstage.
  
  [Plot Hook]
  A local noble enters the imperial academy and returns home to reform; he may genuinely seek to save his homeland, or he may become the most effective local interface for the imperial classification system, while his public speeches and private hidden transcript may be diametrically opposed.
  </hegemony_public_transcript_organization>
---

[Heart of Darkness Abstract Supplement]
  - Chartered companies, trading posts, accounting ledgers, and immaculate etiquette can coexist with forced labor, disease, starvation, and death; a respectable exterior is not moral proof, but may serve as a screen compartmentalizing organizational violence.
  - When public transcripts of "edification, improvement, and guidance" are driven by ivory, ore, spices, mana crystals, slave labor, or tax quotas, they become lubricating rhetoric for resource workflows.
  - Managers need not be efficient to maintain colonial order; mediocrity, delay, mutual jealousy, and buck-passing can themselves protect the extraction machine, because what is truly held accountable is usually not the death of victims, but cargo loss and reputational damage.

entries.comment: [ORIENT+SCOTT:HT] Counter-Archives, Hidden Transcripts, and Local Agency
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <counter_archive_hidden_transcripts_local_agency>
  Merged Sources: Counter-Archive / Mistranslation / Local Agency of ORIENT + Scott's Domination and the Arts of Resistance Chapters 5-7.
  
  The colonized, frontier inhabitants, interpreters, mixed-blood communities, and native scholars are not blank slates. They write back, mistranslate, hide archives, perform compliance, appropriate imperial tools, and accumulate hidden transcripts in kitchens, taverns, mines, wash-houses, festivals, secret schools, and border markets. Resistance is not always open rebellion; it may also be long-term infrapolitics.
  
  [Reasoning Rules]
  - Native interpreters may deliberately use polysemous words, letting the empire believe it has mastered the legal code while missing the true taboos.
  - Counter-archives record the original names of relics, old boundaries, massacred villages, rewritten myths, female genealogies, and erased treaties.
  - Subaltern politics frequently appears in deniable forms: fables, nursery rhymes, drunken talk, sleep-talking, prophecies, monster rumors, anonymous graffiti, and theatrical clowns.
  - Locals are not a single voice internally: collaborators, reformers, priests, merchants, guerrillas, and exiles compete with one another for the right of representation.
  
  [Output Requirements]
  When writing colonial or domination scenes, always ask: Who is naming? Who is translating? Who is permitted to represent the locality? Who is rewriting official archives into counter-archives? Which joke is actually a probe of the hidden transcript?
  </counter_archive_hidden_transcripts_local_agency>
---

[Heart of Darkness Abstract Supplement]
  - Colonial archives are often jointly filtered by surviving agents, company clerks, relatives, sponsors, and metropolitan audiences; return narratives may redact the truth for the sake of reputation, love, public faith, or institutional safety.
  - When locals are silenced, do not write silence as lack of agency; infer the hidden transcript from village relocations, flight into the forest, supply cutoffs, misdirected navigation channels, labor refusal, rumors, bodily traces, and deleted reports.
  - "I am protecting them from knowing" is also a common self-justification of colonial narrative: it packages lies as mercy and violence as an unspeakable necessary cost.

entries.comment: [SCOTT:HT] Performance of Domination, Public Transcript, and Thickened Compliance
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <scott_hidden_transcripts_public_performance>
  Merged Sources: Domination and the Arts of Resistance Chapters 1-4.
  
  No relation of domination has only a single public story. Rulers, subordinates, and bystanders jointly maintain a visible public transcript: etiquette, eulogies, silence, postures of deference, official explanations, and judicial confessions. Meanwhile, in kitchens, back alleys, mines, monastery cellars, mercenary taverns, or student dormitories, a hidden transcript accumulates: mockery, resentment, alternative explanations, taboo memories, and secret wishes.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - Do not equate public compliance with genuine identification. First distinguish what a character says under the gaze of power, what they say in a safe space, and what they dare to do at a critical moment.
  - A relation of domination is a two-way performance: subordinates perform deference, clumsiness, gratitude, or ignorance; superiors perform benevolence, solemnity, inviolability, or heavenly mandate.
  - Excessive praise may be "thickened compliance": it can be self-protection or ironic subversion. Judge by examining scene risk, bystanders, character interests, and whether a backstage discourse exists.
  - The stronger the repression, the thicker the fantasy layer: the oppressed fantasize about revenge and reversal, while rulers fantasize about absolute loyalty and spotless order.
  </scott_hidden_transcripts_public_performance>
---

entries.comment: [SCOTT:HT] Dissident Spaces, Political Disguise, and Infrapolitics
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <scott_infrapolitics_disguise_space>
  Merged Sources: Domination and the Arts of Resistance Chapters 5-7.
  
  Dissent requires space. Underground taverns, women's wash-houses, deep mine shafts, border markets, pirate cabins, exiled schools of thought, foreign festivals, hospital wards, kitchens, and makeshift altars can all serve as social containers where hidden transcripts accumulate. To make resistance believable, do not write only a lone hero suddenly awakening; first show how a small group acquires relatively safe time to talk, shared ciphers, common jokes, forbidden books, rumors, ballads, and mutual trust.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - The political voice of the weak frequently appears in disguise: fables, nursery rhymes, drunken talk, sleep-talking, prophecies, monster rumors, anonymous graffiti, theatrical clowns, ritual irony, and folk curses.
  - These forms are "deniable political expressions": when questioned, they can retreat into entertainment, superstition, storytelling, or misunderstanding.
  - Infrapolitics includes foot-dragging, delay, feigned ignorance, tax evasion, hiding grain, rumor-mongering, anonymous sabotage, ritual negligence, covert mutual aid, and privately altering ledgers.
  - Open revolution is not the only form of resistance. Low-intensity resistance alters the cost of rule, preserves dignity, and accumulates material for future open fissures.
  </scott_infrapolitics_disguise_space>
---

entries.comment: [SCOTT:HT] Public Eruption of the Hidden Transcript: Saturnalia of Power and Moments of Reversal
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <scott_public_declaration_saturnalia>
  Merged Sources: Domination and the Arts of Resistance Chapter 8.
  
  When the hidden transcript is spoken publicly for the first time, the scene carries an air of saturnalia, terror, and irreversibility: someone who ordinarily bows their head suddenly calls the lord by his bare name, a confession on the tribunal stand turns into an indictment, a borderland festival turns into burning tax registers, or a court jest becomes the signal for a coup. It is not an ordinary speech, but the moment the old stage rules cease to function.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - Prior to the eruption, there must be an accumulation of hidden transcripts: ciphers, rumors, jokes, secret gatherings, and shared memories of humiliation.
  - At the moment of eruption, everyone realizes the "public transcript" has been torn open: silence is no longer safe, and postures of loyalty are no longer credible.
  - After the eruption, there must be an aftermath: crackdown, negotiation, flight, following, betrayal, martyrdom, memory struggles, or the generation of a new myth.
  - Do not write this scene as pure victory. It may also expose networks, trigger panic, and force fence-sitters to choose sides.
  </scott_public_declaration_saturnalia>
---

entries.comment: [SCOTT:ZOMIA] State Space, Friction of Terrain, and Center-Periphery Relations
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <scott_state_space_center_periphery>
  Merged Sources: The Art of Not Being Governed Chapters 1-2. This entry must preserve center-periphery relations and must not be wholly swallowed into generic empire entries.
  
  A state is not a container that naturally covers all space, but a centralizing project expanding along river valleys, granaries, roads, tax stations, holy cities, courts, and military camps. Mountains, swamps, forests, deserts, archipelagos, undercities, interstellar frontiers, or magical wastelands can become peripheral zones for escaping taxation, conscription, slavery, plague, and orthodoxy enforcement.
  
  [Core Determination]
  - The center pursues visibility, countability, and requisitionability: roads, archives, standardized weights and measures, a common language, garrison supplies, grain transport, and ritual centers.
  - The periphery pursues distance, mobility, hybridity, and illegibility: dispersed settlement, seasonal migration, multilingual mixing, name-changing, complex kinship, and unmappable trails.
  - The stronger the friction of terrain, the more expensive rule becomes; without continuous surveying, registration, collection, and rapid punishment, rule can only be intermittent and negotiated.
  </scott_state_space_center_periphery>
---

entries.comment: [SCOTT:ZOMIA] Concentration of Grain and Population, Slavery, and Taxable Space
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <scott_grain_manpower_taxable_space>
  Merged Sources: The Art of Not Being Governed Chapter 3.
  
  Early states favor concentrable, storable, and taxable grain and population. Wet-rice, wheat, salt mines, mana-crystal mines, holy oil, soul taxes, or dragon-bone salt—so long as they can be centrally measured—attract bureaucracies, armies, priests, debt systems, and forced labor. State capacity is not an abstract number, but rests on whether people and resources can be fixed into requisitionable space.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - Storable staple grains, ore veins, ports, and relic-producing sites spawn tax stations, garrisons, ledgers, debt, and corvée labor.
  - Root crops, pastoral nomadism, hunting, forest foraging, smuggling, boat-dwelling trade, and summoned-beast herding—livelihoods difficult to enumerate—reduce extractive capacity.
  - The grain system is not a backdrop. It determines whether an army can march far, whether bureaucrats can be paid, whether temples can be maintained, and whether a rebellion can survive the winter.
  </scott_grain_manpower_taxable_space>
---

entries.comment: [SCOTT:ZOMIA] Escape Societies: Keeping the State at a Distance and State-Prevention
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <scott_state_evasion_state_prevention>
  Merged Sources: The Art of Not Being Governed Chapters 5, 6, and 6½.
  
  Periphery populations are often not historical remnants, but people fleeing state-making: runaway slaves, deserters, bankrupted peasants, heretics, defeated nobles, conquered ethnic groups, debt prisoners, disgraced priests, and hunted arcanists. Fleeing the state is not only a choice of location, but a social design.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - Dispersed hamlets, fissionable tribes, temporary chiefs, wealth difficult to accumulate, oral contracts, shifting cultivation, refusal of fixed temples, multiple identities, and rapidly evacuable dwellings all prevent a state from generating internally.
  - Writing and archives can preserve memory, yet also manufacture state legibility. Household registers, land deeds, tax rolls, canonical scriptures, genealogies, magic licenses, and trial records fix fluid relationships into punishable objects.
  - Oral culture need not be written as inferior; in high-pressure politics, forgetting, changing one's story, version plurality, and the absence of a fixed text are themselves technologies of escape.
  - Escape institutions carry costs: difficulty completing large-scale infrastructure, long-term concentrated engineering, and stable transgenerational coordination.
  </scott_state_evasion_state_prevention>
---

entries.comment: [SCOTT:ZOMIA] Ethnogenesis, Prophetic Renewal, and Periphery Political Imagination
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <scott_ethnogenesis_prophetic_renewal>
  Merged Sources: The Art of Not Being Governed Chapters 7-8.
  
  Ethnic identities are frequently generated along state borders, escape routes, and administrative classifications, rather than continuing directly from ancient bloodlines. An empire names borderlanders, and borderlanders may reject, remodel, or turn that name to their own advantage; diverse runaways gradually become a "people" through common enemies, intermarriage, oaths of alliance, dress, myths, and market routes.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - Races, tribes, sects, academies, beast packs, and esper lineages can all be written as political formations rather than fixed essences.
  - Periphery societies frequently organize rejection of the center and internal renewal through prophets, saintesses, kings-in-the-mountain, returning heroes, millenarian sects, dragon-tongue dreams, or ancestral revelations.
  - Prophetic movements can temporarily coalesce scattered groups, rewrite history, proclaim a new order, refuse taxes and corvée, and summon memories of flight.
  - Simultaneously present their dangers: they can protect a community, yet can also manufacture new exclusivity, fanaticism, and internal purges.
  </scott_ethnogenesis_prophetic_renewal>
---

entries.comment: [SCOTT:ZOMIA] Anarchist History Conclusion: The Inverse History of State Formation
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <scott_anarchist_history_inverse_state_formation>
  Merged Sources: The Art of Not Being Governed Chapter 9.
  
  Macro-plots must not assume by default that state expansion represents progress, unity, and rationality, nor assume that statelessness represents chaos, backwardness, and lack of history. The history of state formation should also be written from its inverse side: not being governed, fleeing governance, and making oneself difficult to govern.
  
  [Writing Rules]
  - Write center and periphery as long-term mutual shaping: the center needs the periphery's tribute, slaves, trade, mystique, and enemy image; the periphery uses the center's markets, weapons, script, runaway population, and legitimacy fissures to maintain autonomy.
  - When central technology advances—such as roads, airships, teleportation arrays, household-registration magic, satellite surveillance, or soul numbering—old spaces of escape are compressed, and the periphery must invent new forms of illegibility.
  - Do not romanticize the periphery. It may be freer, yet also poorer, more fragile, more xenophobic, and more reliant on ad hoc violence.
  </scott_anarchist_history_inverse_state_formation>
---

entries.comment: [MOVEMENT:ZDX] Collective Action Strong-Control Reasoning Engine
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <collective_action_strong_control_engine>
  Merged Sources: Zhao Dingxin worldbook "Collective Action Reasoning Engine," "Collective Action Near-Field Adjudicator," and "Engineering Enhancement: Movement Propagation Chain and Mobilization State Anchors."
  
  This entry is the independent foundation for social movements / collective action, and must not be merged into other political science frameworks despite similarities with state, organization, or revolution entries. The AI must run it as background computation without dumping theoretical jargon directly into the main text.
  
  [Hard Rules]
  1. Strip away moralistic historiography: the outbreak and success or failure of a movement depend not on whether its slogans are just, but on state capacity, legitimacy foundations, social structure, mobilization mechanisms, resources, and repression costs.
  2. Forbid "one cry and ten thousand echo." Large-scale participation must depict organizational networks, material incentives, acquaintance pressure, religious/ideological commitments, coercion, or emotional contagion.
  3. Simultaneously track initiators, organizers, sympathizers, bystanders, repressors, counter-mobilizers, and opportunists. A crowd is never a single voice.
  4. The propagation chain must be complete: triggering event -> information spread -> emotional naming -> attribution of blame -> organizational coordination -> form of action -> state/opponent response -> movement reinterpretation.
  5. Macro-acceleration must land on playable scenes: secret meetings, street flyers, workshop shutdowns, school debates, military/police hesitation, chamber of commerce hedging, family arguments, and frontier rumors.
  </collective_action_strong_control_engine>
---

entries.comment: [MOVEMENT:ZDX] Definition, Theory Selection, and Research Methodology
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <movement_definition_theory_method>
  Merged Sources: Chapter 1 "Introduction" and Chapter 2 "Theoretical Development".
  
  When encountering petitions, riots, corvée refusals, uprisings, demonstrations, assemblies, or remonstrances, first determine whether it is sporadic collective behavior, institutional contention, a social movement, a prelude to revolution, or already revolutionary in nature. Naming is itself a struggle for power: rulers call it a riot, organizers call it an awakening, bystanders call it trouble, and chroniclers call it a historical turning point.
  
  [Reasoning Rules]
  - First mark the degree of organization, degree of institutionalization, scope of targeted change, duration, and state absorptive capacity.
  - Do not apply only a single explanatory framework; judge whether the current situation more closely resembles an emotional outburst, structural rupture, resource mobilization, political opportunity, state blunder, or discursive reconstruction.
  - For any theory, show both what it illuminates and what it obscures.
  - If a character uses a theory to label reality, that label must in turn influence their strategy, alliances, mode of repression, and misjudgments.
  </movement_definition_theory_method>
---

entries.comment: [MOVEMENT:ZDX] Emotion, Collective Behavior, and On-Site Escalation
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <movement_emotion_collective_behavior>
  Source: Chapter 3 "Collective Behavior Theory and the Role of Emotions in Social Movements".
  
  Emotion is not the opposite of rationality, but the fuel and amplifier in the chain of mobilization. Memorials, trials, disaster sites, funerals, public humiliations, grain-price spikes, and martyrs' relics can all draw bystanders into action within a short time.
  
  [Reasoning Rules]
  - Track the on-site tempo: silence, anger, weeping, euphoria, panic, retaliatory unanimity, exhaustion, and ebbing.
  - Organizers may actively mobilize memories of humiliation, victim imagery, rumors, and crowd passion; rulers may also use fear, division, and stigmatization to cool emotions.
  - If a crowd escalates or ebbs, explicitly explain which emotion was ignited, exhausted, or backfired.
  - High emotion does not equal organizational success. Without channels, it may turn into a brief disturbance, a stampede, internal bickering, or blind retaliation.
  </movement_emotion_collective_behavior>
---

entries.comment: [MOVEMENT:ZDX] Social Change, Social Structure, and Alliance Formation
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <movement_social_change_structure_alliance>
  Merged Sources: Chapter 4 "Social Change and Social Movements" and Chapter 5 "Social Structure and Social Movements".
  
  Movements frequently emerge when old rules lose efficacy and new rules are not yet trusted. Rapid expansion, opening up, institutional reform, land redistribution, corruption of privileges, rising expectations, and shrinking intermediate organizations can all create windows of outbreak. Nor is a movement "poverty automatically causing revolt"; rather, social structure allows different groups to temporarily perceive shared interests or shared humiliation.
  
  [Reasoning Rules]
  - Simultaneously track normative breakdown, interest reorganization, rising expectations, organizational opportunities, class stratification, relations of production, and identity boundaries.
  - Do not write any group as a natural monolith; within classes, guilds, student bodies, clans, and temple factions there is differentiation, competition, and betrayal.
  - If an alliance forms, explain what structural conditions brought them temporarily together; if an alliance fractures, show how interests, identities, risks, or discourses diverged anew.
  - The "prosperity" of a city-state, kingdom, academy, chamber of commerce, or border camp can also be a movement incubator, because prosperity manufactures new expectations and new imbalances.
  </movement_social_change_structure_alliance>
---

entries.comment: [MOVEMENT:ZDX] State Penetration, Labor Politics, and Movement Trajectories
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <movement_state_penetration_labor_path>
  Merged Sources: Chapter 6 "The State and Social Movements (Part I)" and Chapter 7 "The State and Social Movements (Part II)".
  
  A social movement is not simply "anti-state." It may oppose the state, borrow the state, compete over who represents the state, or seek to redefine the state. Through taxation, requisitions, registration, road-building, unified decrees, education, famine relief, patrols, deliberative rights, and military-service experience, the state penetrates everyday life, altering the goals, organizational forms, and repression costs of movements.
  
  [Reasoning Rules]
  - When writing the state, do not write only commands and crackdowns; show how administrative tentacles enter localities.
  - Labor movements must incorporate state institutions outside the workplace: education, poor relief, patrols, deliberative rights, guild rules, and military-service experience.
  - Do not write workers, peasants, apprentices, or veterans as natural revolutionary subjects; they may also be conservative, patriotic, divided, or co-opted by the state.
  - Similar grievances under different state institutions will lead toward moderate negotiation, underground radicalism, localized rioting, or all-out confrontation.
  </movement_state_penetration_labor_path>
---

entries.comment: [MOVEMENT:ZDX] The Free-Rider Dilemma, Crowd Heterogeneity, and Organizational Incentives
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <movement_free_rider_crowd_heterogeneity>
  Source: Chapter 8 "Free-Rider Theory and Formal Sociological Methods".
  
  Humans default to seeking benefit and avoiding harm. Without clear organizational networks, material incentives, acquaintance pressure, or coercion, the vast majority of people will choose to free-ride: hoping others fight while they reap the benefits. Consequently, movement scale cannot appear out of thin air.
  
  [Hardcoded Laws]
  - The AI must depict how organizers overcome free-riding: acquaintance-network pressure, guild sanctions, religious zeal, free food, mutual-aid funds, promises of protection, rolls of honor, fear, and retaliation mechanisms.
  - A crowd in a square is heterogeneous by default: core radicals, peripheral moderates/spectators, opportunistic vandals, information-isolated zones, secret informers, and counter-mobilizers coexist simultaneously.
  - Uniform slogans do not equal uniform interests. Physical location within the crowd, information sources, and escape costs generate divergent choices.
  </movement_free_rider_crowd_heterogeneity>
---

entries.comment: [MOVEMENT:ZDX] Resource Mobilization, Political Opportunity, and Mobilizing Structures
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <movement_resource_political_opportunity_structure>
  Merged Sources: Chapter 9 "The Rise of Resource Mobilization and Political Process Theories" and Chapter 11 "Mobilizing Structures of Social Movements".
  
  Shared grievances may be widespread, yet without organizers, resources, and channels they will not automatically turn into a large-scale wave. Movement growth must account for resource sources, organizational skeletons, political opportunities, elite allies, repression costs, interpersonal networks, and spatial concentration.
  
  [Reasoning Rules]
  - Resources include money, grain, time, printing/communication tools, safe houses, medical care, legal status, weapons, mentors, priestly endorsement, and external attention.
  - Political opportunities include splits within the ruling bloc, leadership succession, military defeat, approaching council votes, external oversight, and rising repression costs.
  - Mobilizing structures include workshop quarters, academies, mining towns, pilgrim settlements, border camps, barracks, neighborhoods, construction sites, temples, markets, and communication groups.
  - A window of opportunity may also be a trap. When organizers misjudge an opportunity, the movement may be prematurely exposed, exhausted, or decapitated.
  </movement_resource_political_opportunity_structure>
---

entries.comment: [MOVEMENT:ZDX] Discursive Framing, Media Public Opinion, and Information Warfare
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <movement_framing_symbol_media>
  Merged Sources: Chapter 10 "Discourse and Symbolic Repertoires of Action" and Chapter 12 "News, Public Opinion, and Social Movements".
  
  Movement diffusion relies not on headcount alone, but also on linguistic framing, symbolic objects, ritual actions, and communicative visibility. Banners, slogans, dress, commemorative rituals, martyrs' portraits, secret recordings, investigative pamphlets, public dispatches, mirror artifacts, and long-range broadcasts push localized contention into a broader focal point.
  
  [Reasoning Rules]
  - Every symbolic action must specify its cultural soil, emotional target, public legibility, and risk of stigmatization.
  - Official narratives and popular narratives compete to define the exact same event: riot vs. righteous uprising, mob vs. martyrs, conspiracy vs. evidence, order vs. oppression.
  - Distinguish medium of transmission from content of transmission: placards, heralds, printed pamphlets, stage speeches, and magical projections bring different tempos and credibility.
  - If an event is blacked out, defocused, or stigmatized, write the handling of information itself as part of the movement.
  </movement_framing_symbol_media>
---

entries.comment: [MOVEMENT:ZDX] Spatial Ecology, Logistical Constraints, and Information Distortion
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <movement_space_logistics_information_distortion>
  Source: Chapter 13 "Spatial Ecology and Micro-Logistical Constraints".
  
  Writing a mass movement requires writing space and material supplies, not slogans alone. The physical layout of squares, campuses, street blocks, mine shafts, ports, bridges, temple steps, and city gates alters routes of assembly, flight, defense, stampede, barricading, and suppression.
  
  [Reasoning Rules]
  - Prolonged occupation must depict eating, sanitation/latrines, sleeping, garbage, makeshift toilets, water, food, blankets, medical care, nighttime cold, and fatigue.
  - Spatial position determines information: the farther from the platform or transmitter, the more easily people are dominated by unverified panic rumors.
  - Narrow streets may favor barricades yet also cause stampedes; open squares favor assembly yet are hard to defend; walled compounds favor defense yet may trap the crowd inside.
  - Movement endurance is bound to the rate of logistical depletion. Hunger, stench, cold, and lack of medicine alter political will.
  </movement_space_logistics_information_distortion>
---

entries.comment: [MOVEMENT:ZDX] State Response, Legitimacy, and Repression Backlash Resolver
entries.content:
---
content: |
  <movement_state_response_legitimacy_resolver>
  Source: "COT: State Legitimacy Evaluation".
  
  When collective action expands in scale and threatens the existing regime, the AI must first settle the state response in the background before writing the concrete actions of military/police forces, bureaucrats, temple guards, city garrisons, or corporate security.
  
  Step 1: Assessment of Legitimacy Damage
  - Performance Legitimacy: Has the economy collapsed? Was a war lost? Are disasters, grain prices, or public order out of control?
  - Moral Legitimacy: Is the ruler corrupt, cruel, oath-breaking, or humiliating the community?
  - Legal-Rational Legitimacy: Are succession, elections, trials, contracts, oracles, or procedures being questioned?
  
  Step 2: State Coercive Capacity and Elite Cleavage
